stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

# task-128a579e: stamp the marker silhouette into the background

## Confirmed rule
A sparse, distinctive marker-colored motif acts as a stencil. Find translated locations where every stencil cell is currently the background color, then recolor those cells to the marker color. Preserve the original motif and every other cell. The copy retains the exact silhouette and orientation; do not rotate/reflect it. Background/noise cells outside the stencil stay unchanged.

The fill color is the original motif color (2 in the accepted test, 8 in demo 1, 6 in demo 2). The motif shape and palette vary by instance, so extract the complete seed-cell coordinate set from the current input rather than reusing a memorized stencil. Search all valid translations, including ones overlapping the motif's bounding rectangle if the stencil positions themselves are background; avoid candidates whose stencil intersects any non-background cell.

## Evidence from this instance
- Demo 1: random 0/4 field and a distinct color-8 silhouette; output preserved that seed silhouette and stamped copies of its shape into matching all-zero locations as color 8.
- Demo 2: random 0/4 field and color-6 silhouette at rows 4–7, cols 10–12 (zero-based). Its shape by bounding-box rows is `6.6 / 666 / 666 / ..6`; output repeats that silhouette in all-zero matches as 6, preserving the source and unrelated 0/4 cells.
- Accepted test: 21x29, background 9, marker 2. Seed cells (zero-based) were `(3,9),(4,8),(5,7),(6,6),(7,5),(7,7)`, a six-cell stencil. Every all-9 translated instance was filled with 2. Matching stencil top-left coordinates (zero-based): `(0,10),(0,14),(2,14),(2,24),(3,18),(5,10),(5,14),(5,23),(6,13),(6,19),(7,2),(10,13),(10,19),(11,9),(13,13)`. All other cells remained exactly as input. Submission was confirmed CORRECT with zero wrong attempts.

## Reliable procedure and pitfalls
1. Identify marker color and background from the full grid; locate the distinctive sparse seed motif, separating it from random background speckles.
2. Represent the entire motif as offsets from its top-left bounding-box corner. Preserve holes: the copy is an exact silhouette, not a filled rectangle.
3. At every possible translation, require all stencil-offset cells to equal the background. Recolor just those cells to the seed color; leave every other location untouched.
4. Apply matches without allowing newly recolored copies to generate extra overlapping candidates; determine candidate locations against the original input.
5. Validate dimensions and candidate positions. A generic pattern-matching pass on the six-cell test stencil initially falsely included `(16,1)` due to an incorrect row-range bound; correct valid-origin bounds use `r <= H - motif_height` and `c <= W - motif_width`. The accepted complete search found 15 copies listed above.

This evidence supports exact silhouette copying into matching background positions across the two demos and accepted test. Re-derive the seed silhouette every time; do not assume the demo's colors or template shape recur."
}
